einzeiler: Rosalee Mayeux on modeling life, cancer survival, and finding stand-up comedy.
kurzfassung: Rosalee Mayeux shares her journey from working as a fashion model in New York and Paris to raising two boys as a single mother in Los Angeles. She discusses how surviving a severe cancer diagnosis inspired her to transition into stand-up comedy and embrace life's absurdities. Throughout the conversation, she highlights the healing power of humor and the importance of not taking oneself too seriously.
stichpunkte: Started her career as a high-fashion model in New York and Paris before transitioning into acting and comedy
Navigated the challenges of raising two boys as a single mother in Los Angeles while dealing with chaotic neighborhood surroundings
Faced a life-threatening triple-negative breast cancer diagnosis and used humor to get through harsh treatments
Discovered stand-up comedy later in life after a friend secretly put her name on an open mic list
Emphasizes that the ability to laugh at oneself is a true sign of mental health
Released her debut comedy special, Model Mom, capturing her first five years of comedic storytelling
Maintains a 36-year involvement with Al-Anon, relying on a supportive sponsor and community for life guidance

beschreibung:
Before comedy, Rosalee Mayeux walked the runways of New York and Paris as a high-fashion model. Then came cancer, single motherhood, and a total reinvention — this time, with a microphone in hand. On this encore episode of Comedy Saved Me, host Lynn Hoffman talks with Rosalee about turning survival into material, raising two boys in LA with equal parts chaos and humor, and building her debut comedy special, Model Mom, out of the wreckage and wonder of real life.

Rosalee opens up about using comedy to process illness, self-acceptance, and the messiness of motherhood — and why laughing at the hard stuff doesn’t minimize it, it makes it survivable. It’s a conversation about resilience, reinvention, and the community that comedy builds around us when we need it most.
